title: The Directed Rule Reaches the Interior: an Odd Number of Interior Degree-1 Rooms (n = 2 Tucker)
description: The sperner-mathlib4-oq-02 program proves Tucker's lemma from an abstract door-counting (path-following / handshaking) engine: SpernerTuckerPathFollowing.exists_interior_degree_one turns two hypotheses on a door graph — an EVEN total number of degree-1 endpoints (handshaking) and an ODD number of BOUNDARY degree-1 endpoints — into a degree-1 endpoint that is INTERIOR, the Tucker witness room. Its first concrete instantiation (SpernerTuckerHexagonSignFlipEngine) fired the engine on the UNDIRECTED Sperner sign-flip door graph and produced only a DIAGNOSTIC: the engine's endpoint is always a boundary edge of the opposite hemisphere, never interior (the undirected door graph is all cycles). The brute classification (probe_ft_nested_bruteforce.py) then proved WHY — no undirected edge-local rule can supply an odd full-circle seed (all are negation-symmetric, so the antipodal 6-cycle pairs their doors even) — and singled out the ORIENTED directed pos→neg sign door rule door(x→y) ⇔ sgn x = 0 ∧ sgn y = 1 (mask 0x00cc) as the essentially-unique closer, whose two abstract blades (per-triangle ≤ 1 directed door; odd full-circle count) were verified in the sibling entry oq-07. This entry runs those blades through the engine's parity split ON THE DISC ROOMS and reaches the conclusion the sign-flip engine could not: an odd — hence non-zero — number of degree-1 rooms whose single door is INTERIOR. Each triangle T_i = (centre d, v_i, v_{i+1}) is a room oriented d→v_i→v_{i+1}→d; roomDoor counts directed doors on all three oriented sides (= hexDirTri, so ≤ 1 by room_door_le_one), intDoor counts the two interior spokes (d→v_i, v_{i+1}→d), bdDoor the boundary edge (v_i→v_{i+1}). A degree-1 room has roomDoor = 1; it is interior when intDoor = 1 and boundary when bdDoor = 1. The three parity facts, all by kernel decide over the 256 antipodal labellings: total_deg1_even (total degree-1 rooms EVEN, values ∈ {4,6} — handshaking), boundary_deg1_odd (boundary degree-1 rooms ODD, values ∈ {1,3} — the odd seed, matching full_dir_count_odd), and handshake_split (total = interior + boundary, since roomDoor ≤ 1 makes every degree-1 room interior-XOR-boundary). From these the mechanism theorem interior_deg1_odd derives — by parity, NOT re-enumeration — that the number of INTERIOR degree-1 rooms is ODD; interior_deg1_eq_three sharpens it to exactly 3; and exists_interior_room extracts the witness FROM the parity count (Finset.card_pos on interior_deg1_pos). Contrast SpernerTuckerHexagonSignFlipEngine, whose interior endpoint count is 0: orientation moves the odd seed from a hemisphere to the whole circle, and the resulting even/odd handshake pushes an odd, positive count of endpoints into the INTERIOR. Honest status: a positive scoping result — the door-counting parity now FORCES an interior degree-1 room to exist, the structural conclusion the undirected reduction provably could not deliver. It is NOT a full proof of n = 2 Tucker: an interior degree-1 room is the terminal room of the Freund–Todd signed pivot, and its interior directed door coincides with a genuine complementary edge (λ u = −λ v) for only half of these rooms, so identifying the terminal room with the Tucker witness still needs the pivot-connectivity argument (the bare existence of a complementary edge is machine-checked separately in the sibling oq-06 / SpernerTuckerHexagonComplementaryEdge). What is new here is the mechanism: the oriented door count drives the even/odd handshake to a non-zero INTERIOR endpoint count, which the entire undirected edge-local class cannot. 0 axioms, 0 sorries (propext / Classical.choice / Quot.sound only — plain decide, no Lean.ofReduceBool).

overview.historicalContext: Tucker's lemma (Albert W. Tucker, 1945) is the combinatorial heart of the Borsuk–Ulam theorem: an antipodally-symmetric triangulation of Bⁿ labelled into {±1,…,±n}, antipodal on the boundary, always has a complementary edge (endpoints k, −k). The constructive proofs (Freund–Todd 1981; Prescott–Su 2005) are ORIENTED path-following: follow a directed path of almost-complementary simplices from a forced boundary endpoint to an interior complementary one. The sperner-mathlib4-oq-02 program formalizes that door-counting argument abstractly (SpernerTuckerPathFollowing) and on the concrete hexagon + centre triangulation of B². The first concrete instantiation of the engine (SpernerTuckerHexagonSignFlipEngine) applied it to the undirected sign-flip door graph and got only a diagnostic — the endpoint lands on the antipodal boundary, never interior — because that graph is all cycles. A complete finite classification of all 2^16 undirected edge-local rules then proved no undirected rule can close n = 2 Tucker and singled out the oriented directed pos→neg sign rule as the essentially-unique closer; the sibling entry oq-07 carried that rule and its two abstract blades into Lean.
overview.problemStatement: On the hexagon + centre triangulation of B² (labels {+1,+2,−1,−2} as Fin 4, negL = ![2,3,0,1], sign map sgn = ![0,0,1,1]; six boundary vertices antipodal v_{i+3} = −v_i from three free labels a,b,c; centre label d), fire the abstract path-following engine's parity mechanism on the disc ROOMS under the directed pos→neg door rule. Each room T_i = (d, v_i, v_{i+1}) is oriented d→v_i→v_{i+1}→d; roomDoor counts its directed doors (≤ 1), split into intDoor (the two interior spokes) and bdDoor (the boundary edge). Prove: (1) total_deg1_even — the number of degree-1 rooms (roomDoor = 1) is EVEN; (2) boundary_deg1_odd — the number whose door is on the boundary edge is ODD; (3) handshake_split — total = interior + boundary; and hence (4) interior_deg1_odd / interior_deg1_eq_three / exists_interior_room — the number of degree-1 rooms whose door is on an INTERIOR spoke is odd (exactly 3), so such a room exists, for every antipodal labelling and centre.
overview.proofStrategy: Everything is a finite check over the 4⁴ = 256 antipodal labellings (a,b,c,d) discharged by kernel decide (not native_decide, so no Lean.ofReduceBool) plus elementary parity/omega. The directed indicator dir x y := if x = 0 ∧ y = 1 then 1 else 0 is over ZMod 2. intDoor a b c d i := dir (sgn d) (sgn (V a b c i)) + dir (sgn (V a b c (rot i))) (sgn d) counts the two interior spokes of room i; bdDoor its boundary edge; roomDoor := intDoor + bdDoor (= SpernerTuckerHexagonDirectedSignDoor.hexDirTri), so room_door_le_one is decided. The three room counts are Finset cardinalities #{i : Fin 6 | …} with decidable predicates: total_deg1_even, boundary_deg1_odd and handshake_split are each decided over all 256 labellings. The payoff interior_deg1_odd is then derived NOT by re-enumeration but by the engine's own parity logic: rewrite total_deg1_even to (total % 2 = 0) and boundary_deg1_odd to (boundary % 2 = 1), substitute handshake_split (total = interior + boundary), and omega forces interior % 2 = 1. interior_deg1_pos follows (odd ⇒ ≥ 1) and exists_interior_room extracts a room from Finset.card_pos on that positive count — the witness is produced by the door-counting handshake, mirroring exists_interior_degree_one's own card_pos extraction. interior_deg1_eq_three records the sharp value 3 by decide.
keyInsights: The directed pos→neg sign rule REACHES THE INTERIOR: for every one of the 256 antipodal labellings there are exactly 3 (an odd, positive number of) degree-1 rooms whose single directed door lies on an interior spoke (interior_deg1_eq_three, exists_interior_room). This is the structural conclusion the first engine instantiation (SpernerTuckerHexagonSignFlipEngine) provably could NOT deliver: there the interior endpoint count is 0 and the engine's output is always an antipodal-boundary edge.

The conclusion is DRIVEN BY DOOR-COUNTING, not brute force: interior_deg1_odd is proved from total_deg1_even (handshaking: total degree-1 rooms even), boundary_deg1_odd (odd boundary seed) and handshake_split (total = interior + boundary) by pure parity — even minus odd is odd. This is exactly the mechanism of the abstract engine SpernerTuckerPathFollowing.exists_interior_degree_one, realized on the concrete disc rooms with a POSITIVE interior count.

Orientation is what turns the even/odd handshake in the program's favour: the undirected sign-flip rule has an even boundary count (the antipodal involution pairs its doors) and all-cycles interior (no endpoints), while the directed rule has an odd boundary count (the antipode reverses its doors, oq-07 dir_antipode_reverse) and path interior (degree-1 endpoints), so the handshake pushes an odd, non-zero endpoint count into the interior.

The three sharp value profiles pin the combinatorics exactly: total degree-1 rooms ∈ {4,6}, boundary ∈ {1,3}, interior always = 3. The handshake total = interior + boundary holds pointwise because roomDoor ≤ 1 makes every degree-1 room interior-XOR-boundary.

The whole verification is 0-axiom (propext / Classical.choice / Quot.sound only, no native_decide): plain kernel decide over the finite labelling space and Finset cardinalities keeps the searches inside the kernel's trusted reduction, so 'the directed rule forces an interior room' is machine-checked without the Lean.ofReduceBool trust extension.

sections.title: From the Sign-Flip Diagnostic to Reaching the Interior
sections.summary: The header frames the entry against the first engine instantiation (SpernerTuckerHexagonSignFlipEngine), whose undirected sign-flip door graph fires the engine but lands only on an antipodal-boundary edge — never interior — because it is all cycles. The brute classification proved no undirected rule can supply an odd full-circle seed and singled out the oriented directed pos→neg rule (oq-07). This file runs that rule's blades through the engine's parity split on the disc rooms and reaches an odd, positive count of INTERIOR degree-1 rooms. Honest status: a positive scoping result, not a full proof of n = 2 Tucker — the interior room is the Freund–Todd pivot's terminal room, whose door is a genuine complementary edge only half the time.

sections.title: The Antipodal Labelling Model
sections.summary: negL = ![2,3,0,1] is label negation on {+1,+2,−1,−2} (Fin 4); V a b c = ![a,b,c,negL a,negL b,negL c] gives the six boundary labels from three free labels with the antipodal condition v_{i+3} = −v_i built in; rot i = i+1 is the cyclic successor; sgn = ![0,0,1,1] is the sign map; dir x y := if x = 0 ∧ y = 1 then 1 else 0 is the directed pos→neg door indicator on ZMod 2 sign bits. Identical encoding to the sibling SpernerTuckerHexagonDirectedSignDoor (oq-07).

sections.title: Rooms of the Disc: Interior and Boundary Directed Doors
sections.summary: Each triangle T_i = (centre d, v_i, v_{i+1}) is a room oriented d→v_i→v_{i+1}→d. intDoor a b c d i counts the directed doors on its two INTERIOR spokes (d→v_i, v_{i+1}→d); bdDoor its single BOUNDARY side (v_i→v_{i+1}); roomDoor := intDoor + bdDoor is the total over all three oriented sides (equal to SpernerTuckerHexagonDirectedSignDoor.hexDirTri). room_door_le_one proves every room has ≤ 1 directed door, so a degree-1 room's single door is interior-XOR-boundary.

sections.title: The Three Degree-1 Room Counts
sections.summary: interiorDeg1, boundaryDeg1, totalDeg1 are the Finset cardinalities #{i : Fin 6 | …} of, respectively, the degree-1 rooms whose door is interior (roomDoor = 1 ∧ intDoor = 1), whose door is boundary (roomDoor = 1 ∧ bdDoor = 1), and all degree-1 rooms (roomDoor = 1). These are the concrete-room analogues of the abstract engine's endpoint, boundary-endpoint and total-endpoint counts.

sections.title: The Engine's Parity Mechanism, Forcing an Interior Room
sections.summary: total_deg1_even (total degree-1 rooms even, ∈ {4,6}) is the handshaking half; boundary_deg1_odd (boundary degree-1 rooms odd, ∈ {1,3}) is the odd seed matching full_dir_count_odd; handshake_split (total = interior + boundary) records the interior-XOR-boundary split. From these, interior_deg1_odd derives by pure parity (even − odd = odd) — NOT re-enumeration — that the interior degree-1 room count is odd; interior_deg1_eq_three sharpens it to 3; interior_deg1_pos gives positivity; and exists_interior_room extracts the witness room via Finset.card_pos, the concrete realization of exists_interior_degree_one with a positive interior count. All #print axioms report propext / Classical.choice / Quot.sound only.

conclusion.summary: For the hexagon + centre triangulation of B², this entry fires the abstract path-following engine's parity mechanism on the disc rooms under the directed pos→neg sign door rule and reaches the interior. It proves the three engine hypotheses by kernel decide over all 256 antipodal labellings — total_deg1_even (degree-1 rooms even, ∈ {4,6}), boundary_deg1_odd (boundary degree-1 rooms odd, ∈ {1,3}), handshake_split (total = interior + boundary) — and derives from them, by pure parity rather than re-enumeration, that the number of INTERIOR degree-1 rooms is odd (interior_deg1_odd), exactly 3 (interior_deg1_eq_three), hence positive; exists_interior_room then extracts an interior witness room via Finset.card_pos. This is the structural conclusion the first engine instantiation (SpernerTuckerHexagonSignFlipEngine, interior count 0) provably could not deliver: orientation moves the odd seed to the whole circle and the even/odd handshake pushes a non-zero endpoint count into the interior. Eight theorems, eleven definitions, 0 axioms, 0 sorries (propext / Classical.choice / Quot.sound only, plain decide, no Lean.ofReduceBool).
conclusion.implications: This closes the loop the sign-flip engine left open: the door-counting handshake now FORCES an interior degree-1 room, which the entire undirected edge-local class cannot. It is the concrete realization of exists_interior_degree_one with a positive interior endpoint count, driven by the oriented rule's odd full-circle seed (oq-07 full_dir_count_odd). It does not prove n = 2 Tucker: an interior degree-1 room is the Freund–Todd signed pivot's terminal room, and its interior directed door is a genuine complementary edge (λ u = −λ v) for only half of these rooms, so identifying the terminal room with the Tucker witness still requires the pivot-connectivity argument. The bare existence of a complementary edge at n = 2 is already machine-checked separately (sibling oq-06 / SpernerTuckerHexagonComplementaryEdge); the abstract engine and the odd seed are verified in the parent and oq-07. This file supplies the missing verified link — the mechanism producing a non-zero interior endpoint count.
openQuestions: Identify the terminal interior room with a genuine complementary edge: the interior directed door of a degree-1 room coincides with an antipodal label pair (λ u = −λ v) only half the time, so the pivot-connectivity (Freund–Todd path) that carries the odd boundary seed to a complementary terminal room is the remaining step to turn exists_interior_room into a proof of n = 2 Tucker.

Instantiate the abstract SpernerTuckerPathFollowing.exists_interior_degree_one literally on a SimpleGraph whose degree-1 vertices are these directed-door rooms, so the interior witness is the engine's output rather than a hand-run parity split — the directed analogue of SpernerTuckerHexagonSignFlipEngine.engine_fires but with a genuine interior endpoint.

Generalise the directed rule's interior-room parity from the hexagon to the cross-polytope boundary ∂◊^{n+1} (SpernerTuckerCrossPolytopeBoundary) to seed the dimension recursion of SpernerTuckerInductiveTower.
